title: Scheme-theoretic Frobenius fixed points
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $q=p^a$, and let $X_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and let $\Phi:X\to X$ be the $k$-linear base change of the $q$-power Frobenius of $X_0$ [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. For every integer $m\geq1$, the equalizer fixed scheme [def-trf-fixed-scheme] has the canonical isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)\xrightarrow{\sim}\coprod_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\operatorname{Spec}k,$$
whose inverse on the summand indexed by $y$ is the $k$-point obtained from $y$ by extension of scalars. This is a finite coproduct, and the fixed scheme is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and étale [def-weil-etale-morphism] over $k$. Every fixed point is simple: its local ring in the fixed scheme is $k$, of length one [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. At every fixed $k$-point $x$, the differential on tangent spaces [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] satisfies $d\Phi^m_x=0$ and $1-d\Phi^m_x=1$. If $x$ lies in the smooth locus of $X/k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the graph of $\Phi^m$ and the diagonal meet transversally at $(x,x)$ in a smooth open neighbourhood of $(x,x)$ in $X\times_kX$, with local Serre intersection multiplicity one. Transversality here means that their tangent subspaces sum directly to $T_{(x,x)}(X\times_kX)$; the Serre multiplicity is the alternating sum of the lengths of the local Tor groups [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules].

note: *Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

proof.text: Put $Q=q^m$ and $E=\mathbf F_Q$. By [lem-trf-frobenius-affine-equalizer-presentation], choose finitely many stable model affine charts $U_{0,j}=\operatorname{Spec}A_{0,j}$ and presentations $A_{0,j}=k_0[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/\mathfrak a$. On $U_j=U_{0,j}\times_{k_0}k$, the fixed scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}(B_j/J_j)$ with $B_j/J_j=k[t]/(\mathfrak a_k,t_i^Q-t_i)_i$. By [lem-trf-finite-field-relations-evaluation], this quotient is canonically $\prod_{y\in U_{0,j}(E)}k$, with each factor the evaluation at the scalar-extended point $y$. Here $U_{0,j}(E)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}(\operatorname{Spec}E,U_{0,j})$ by [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and the identification of these points with the $k_0$-algebra maps $A_{0,j}\to E$ of the lemma is [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Each such point equalizes $\Phi^m$ and $1$, since its model coordinates lie in $E$ and hence satisfy $z^Q=z$.

By [def-trf-fixed-scheme], $\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)=X\times_{X\times_kX,(1,\Phi^m),\Delta_X}X$, the equalizer of $\Phi^m$ and $1_X$. Apply [lem-trf-equalizer-point-chart-descent] with $h=\Phi^m$, whose $F$ is then exactly $\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)$, the cover $U_j$, $P=X_0(E)$ and its scalar-extended point family. Membership in a geometric chart $U_j$ is equivalent to membership of $y$ in $U_{0,j}$, by the projection to $X_0$. The evaluation isomorphisms of the preceding step give exactly its hypotheses. The lemma gives the canonical coproduct isomorphism with the prescribed summand maps, finite index set, finiteness, étaleness, and all the local-ring and length-one assertions.

source.place: Steps 0, 2, 3: gluing and finite étale consequences

proof.text: On each chart, the coordinate endomorphism is $t_i\mapsto t_i^Q$, with $Q=p^{am}$ and $am\geq1$. Apply [lem-trf-power-map-smooth-graph-local-data] at a fixed $k$-point. Its first conclusion gives $d\Phi^m_x=0$, $1-d\Phi^m_x=1$, and complementary graph/diagonal tangent images. If $x$ is smooth, its equalizer local ring is $k$ by the preceding step, so its second conclusion gives a smooth open neighbourhood of $(x,x)$ and regular local rings $A,A/I,A/J$ of dimensions $2d,d,d$, with $I+J=\mathfrak m_A$ and $A/(I+J)=k$.

source.place: Step 3: tangent and smooth local geometry

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-regular-local-complementary-quotients-tor] with $r=s=d$ and the graph and diagonal ideals from the preceding step. It gives $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(A/I,A/J)=0$ for $i>0$ and $\operatorname{Tor}^A_0(A/I,A/J)\simeq k$, and alternating length sum $1$. This is the asserted local Serre intersection multiplicity; together with the complementary tangent images and smooth neighbourhood it proves the remaining smooth-locus conclusions. The cited lemmas include empty point sets, zero generators, and $d=0$.
